title: PTSD — Traumatic Stress >1 Month After Stabbing
patient: 35-year-old male, stabbed during knife robbery 5 weeks ago, 20 sutures, no organ damage, quick physical recovery
misdiagnosis: Acute Stress Disorder (same symptoms but <1 month duration; this patient is at 5 weeks = PTSD)
hpi: 35-year-old male presents to office with anxiety. Stabbed during knife robbery 5 weeks ago. Required 20 sutures; no major organ damage; quick physical recovery. Reports can't stop thinking about the attack, nightmares, intrusive images of the robber. Avoids going out at night even with family/friends (fear of re-assault). Irritable with family. Hypervigilant ('always looking over my shoulder'). Difficulty sleeping. Calling in sick to work frequently. Symptoms present every day since the incident.

missed.why: Assess how the patient is presenting — anxious, hypervigilant, eye contact, psychomotor agitation.
Mental status exam is the physical exam for psychiatric chief concerns. Assess affect, thought content, cognition, insight.
Rule out medical causes of anxiety — anemia, infection. Standard screening before starting psychiatric medication.
Hyperthyroidism perfectly mimics anxiety. Must rule out before committing to primary psychiatric diagnosis. Given the Graves case immediately prior, this should be reflexive.
Electrolytes, renal function. Hyponatremia must be corrected before starting SSRI/SNRI (SIADH risk). Baseline creatinine for drug dosing.
Evidence-based psychotherapy for PTSD: CBT, CPT (cognitive processing therapy), prolonged exposure therapy, EMDR. USMLE translates all of these as referral to psych/psychology.
First-line pharmacotherapy for PTSD. Paroxetine and sertraline are FDA-approved. USMLE expects BOTH psychotherapy AND pharmacotherapy to be offered.

dsm5Criteria.criterionA: Directly experienced threatened death (stabbed during robbery). MET.
dsm5Criteria.criterionB_intrusion: Intrusive memories, nightmares, intrusive images of the robber. MET.
dsm5Criteria.criterionC_avoidance: Won't go out at night, avoids family/friend gatherings. MET.
dsm5Criteria.criterionE_arousal: Hypervigilance ('looking over my shoulder'), sleep disturbance, exaggerated startle. MET.
dsm5Criteria.criterionF_duration: Symptoms persist >1 month (5 weeks). MET — this distinguishes PTSD from acute stress disorder.
dsm5Criteria.criterionG_impairment: Calling in sick to work frequently, social withdrawal. MET.
dsm5Criteria.criterionH_exclusion: Not attributable to substance or medical condition (vitals normal, no co-occurring illness). MET.

ptsdVsASD.acuteStressDisorder: Symptoms last 3 days to 1 month after trauma
ptsdVsASD.thisCase: 5 weeks post-trauma with daily symptoms = PTSD, not acute stress disorder

timing.note: Case timed out before diagnosis and treatment
